channel.title: Reading List on Underkube
channel.description: Recent content in Reading List on Underkube

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (March 23 - April 5, 2026)
item.description: After a refreshing week off on PTO, I’m back with a double-sized edition covering two weeks of interesting finds in the tech world. This update features a heavy focus on the emerging “NanoClaw” ecosystem, several critical supply chain security disclosures, and some fascinating hardware hacks. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure 7 Configuration Changes That Turn a Multi-Homed Host Into a Switch/Router / How to turn anything into a router - Educational deep dives into transforming standard Linux hosts and PCs into functional home routers.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (March 16 - 22, 2026)
item.description: A diverse week featuring deep dives into Btrfs scaling, a flurry of new AI agent control planes, and some critical security updates for CI/CD pipelines. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure FOSDEM 2026 - The Filesystem Diaries: Scaling Btrfs in an Enterprise - A detailed look at the challenges and solutions for employing Btrfs at scale in large organizational environments. Scaling Btrfs to petabytes in production: a 74% cost reduction story - How one team managed to slash infrastructure costs by leveraging Btrfs features for massive data storage.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (March 9 - 15, 2026)
item.description: This week’s collection highlights the rapid advancement of local AI agent infrastructure, critical security advisories for Linux armor, and significant updates across the Kubernetes and FreeBSD ecosystems. AI, Agents & Tools Oh My OpenAgent - An open-source multi-agent orchestration harness designed for autonomous codebase tasks, featuring specialized agents for planning, execution, and verification. CanIRun.ai - A practical tool to determine if your machine has the hardware necessary to run specific AI models locally.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (March 2 to 8, 2026)
item.description: This week’s reading list is a mix of high stakes security post mortems, ranging from the XZ backdoor to recent GitHub Actions exploits, alongside the rapid evolution of the OpenClaw ecosystem and some surprising hardware moves from Apple. AI, Agents & Tools OpenClaw: Our Comprehensive Guide for Beginners A deep dive into the open source framework for building proactive, personalized AI assistants that live in your messaging apps. SumeLabs/clawra OpenClaw as your AI girlfriend or companion.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 23 - Mar 1, 2026)
item.description: This week’s roundup covers a wide range of topics, including the architectural limits of etcd, GPU-initiated networking, the nostalgic design of Apple’s breathing lights, and the surprising persistence of floppy disks in transit systems. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure Why etcd breaks at scale in Kubernetes - A deep dive into the architectural limitations of etcd and how hyperscalers are evolving beyond it. Sympozium (KubeClaw) — Kubernetes-Native Agentic Control Plane / GitHub Repo: A platform for orchestrating AI agents as isolated skill sidecars with ephemeral RBAC.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 16 - 22, 2026)
item.description: This week’s reading list is heavily focused on Kubernetes observability, AI orchestration, and some very handy tools for navigating the modern web. Cloud, Kubernetes & Infrastructure Fatih Koc’s Observability & Infrastructure Series: Kubernetes Security Observability - A guide to establishing effective security observability in your Kubernetes clusters. OpenTelemetry Kubernetes Pipeline - A walkthrough on setting up a robust OpenTelemetry pipeline specifically for Kubernetes. Monitoring with kube-prometheus-stack - A practical tutorial on monitoring using the popular kube-prometheus-stack.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 9 - 15, 2026)
item.description: This week’s roundup features 40 fresh links covering everything from sandboxing AI agents in Kubernetes to benchmarking LLMs in the game Balatro, along with some spicy open-source drama. Cloud & Kubernetes Kubernetes Gateway API Guide / Archive - A complete step-by-step setup guide for the Kubernetes Gateway API. Agent Sandbox - An official Kubernetes SIGs project for sandboxing AI agents. AI Agent Runtimes on GKE / Video - A guide and accompanying video on building secure, scalable, and isolated AI agent runtimes on Google Kubernetes Engine.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Feb 2 - 8, 2026)
item.description: This week is a massive roundup. The AI agent ecosystem is exploding with new tools (and security leaks), while the “privacy & tunneling” toolbox gets a major refill. AI, Agents & Security Moltbook Database Exposure - Wiz reveals a massive breach in “Moltbook” where millions of API keys were exposed. Moltroad - A “Silk Road” for AI agents to list and trade black market items. P*rnhub for Agents - Exactly what it sounds like… but for AI agents.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Jan 26 - Feb 1, 2026)
item.description: While I try to cover everything from budget Kubernetes to BSD tricks, the star of the show this week is of course ClawdBot/MoltBot/OpenClaw. Photo courtesy of Alejandro Martinez :) Cloud & Kubernetes Kubernetes at $2/month - A guide on running a functional Kubernetes cluster for just $2 a month. EmeritOSS Backs MinIO - Chainguard’s EmeritOSS initiative steps in to support MinIO and other “orphaned” open-source projects. Kubernetes GPU Guide - NVIDIA’s official documentation for GPU-accelerated Kubernetes.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Jan 19 - 25, 2026)
item.description: Here is the roundup of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure Exe.dev - A service to spin up instant, publicly accessible virtual machines with persistent disks. Zarf - An open-source tool for declarative software delivery into air-gapped and constrained environments. K3s + Sysbox - A guide on using the Sysbox container runtime with K3s. Cloud Native RAG - A walkthrough on building a fully self-hosted Cloud Native RAG stack with embeddings and vectors.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Jan 5 - 18, 2026)
item.description: I missed last week’s post because I was too busy trying to beat my high score in UEFI Zaxxon. To make it up to you, here is a double-sized roundup covering the last two weeks. Cloud & Kubernetes Kubernetes Dashboard Archiving - A discussion in the Kubernetes SIG-UI group regarding the potential archiving of the Kubernetes Dashboard project. Ingress Controllers Spreadsheet - A comprehensive, community-maintained spreadsheet comparing various Kubernetes Ingress Controllers.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Dec 29, 2025 - Jan 4, 2026)
item.description: I’ve gathered a fresh batch of links to kick off the new year, ranging from Kubernetes networking and BSD tools to security talks from the 39C3 congress. Cloud, BSD & Infrastructure Kubernetes Egress Control with Squid / Hacker News Discussion: A guide on using Squid proxy to control egress traffic in Kubernetes clusters. BSD Tools Collection: A collection of BSD utilities including mfsBSD & mfslinux (minimal memory-based distributions), miniBSD (small footprint FreeBSD), and occambsd (an application of Occam’s razor to FreeBSD).

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Dec 22 - 28, 2025)
item.description: Here is the roundup of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure Debusine Repositories Launch / Main Page: Debian introduces Debusine, a new PPA-like system allowing developers to publish add-on packages with integrated builds and testing. PCI Passthrough in Harvester - A guide on setting up AMD GPUs in Harvester with PCI passthrough. Password Agents - Documentation from systemd.io regarding the implementation and use of Password Agents. DevOps & Tools Snitch - A tool to inspect network connections in a cleaner, more visual way than standard utilities.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Dec 15 - 21, 2025)
item.description: Here is the roundup of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure Kubernetes v1.35 Release - The official announcement for the latest version of Kubernetes. Docker Hardened Images / Catalog: Docker has made its catalog of hardened container images free to use, designed to secure the software supply chain. Why you can’t ping a Kubernetes Service - A technical explanation of why standard ICMP pings don’t work with K8s ClusterIP services.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Dec 8 - 14, 2025)
item.description: Here is the roundup of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure IBM to acquire Confluent - Major industry news as IBM announces its acquisition of the data streaming platform Confluent. Netvisor - An open-source observability agent for Kubernetes that provides visibility into cluster traffic and network calls. Kubeterm - A graphical terminal specifically designed for managing Kubernetes clusters. Ingress Nginx Migration / GitHub Repo: A tool to assist in migrating from the Nginx Ingress Controller to Traefik.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Dec 1 - 7, 2025)
item.description: Here is the list of links for this week: Cloud & Infrastructure AWS re:Invent 2025 - Keynote with Dr. Werner Vogels - The annual keynote from Amazon’s CTO, covering the latest in cloud technology and the “Renaissance Developer”. MinIO is now maintenance mode - Discussion on Reddit regarding the change in development status for the popular object storage server. FreeBSD 15.0-RELEASE Announcement - The latest stable release of the FreeBSD operating system.

item.title: What Edu is Reading This Week (Nov 23-30 2025)
item.description: What Edu is Reading This Week « This space for rent » :D AI, LLMs & Automation Model Context Protocol (MCP) Introduction: Documentation for the Model Context Protocol, an open standard designed to enable AI agents (LLMs) to interact securely and predictably with external tools, APIs, and data. Jules: The Autonomous Agent CLI Extension / Jules in 90 seconds / Jules GitHub Repo: The official page (and a GitHub repository for a Gemini extension) of Jules, an asynchronous coding sidekick, letting developers delegate long-running tasks.

item.title: What Edu is Reading This Week (Nov 17-23 2025)
item.description: What Edu is Reading This Week Plenty of content this week! Cloud Native & Kubernetes Tuning Linux Swap for Kubernetes: A deep-dive article on why and how to correctly configure and tune Linux swap settings when running Kubernetes workloads. Production-Grade Container Deployment with Podman Quadlets: How to deploy and manage containers using Podman and Quadlets, which leverage native systemd unit files for production-ready setups. Security Contexts in Kubernetes: A breakdown of Kubernetes Security Contexts, covering settings like runAsUser, capabilities, and SELinux options to tighten pod security.

item.title: What Edu is Reading This Week (Nov 10-16 2025)
item.description: What Edu is Reading This Week Fifth week in a row! Cloud Native & Kubernetes Ingress-Nginx Controller Retirement (K8s Blog): Official announcement regarding the planned retirement and deprecation of the classic ingress-nginx controller, signaling the industry shift toward the Gateway API. ingress2gateway: A tool from the Kubernetes SIGs to automatically migrate existing Ingress resources to the newer, more powerful Kubernetes Gateway API. Helm Documentation Overview: The official overview page for Helm 4, the package manager for Kubernetes that announced its 4.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Nov 3 - 9, 2025)
item.description: Another week goes by, another collection of links I found interesting… Infrastructure and Operating Systems FreeBSD Officially Supported in OCI Runtime Specification v1.3 - The Open Container Initiative (OCI) Runtime Specification v1.3 officially includes FreeBSD support. This major milestone positions FreeBSD as a first-class platform for cloud-native workloads, leveraging its existing jails technology for container isolation. Incus: Next-Generation Container and VM Manager - Incus is a next-generation system container, application container, and virtual machine manager that provides a user experience similar to a public cloud.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Oct 27 - Nov 2, 2025)
item.description: Another week goes by, another collection of links I found interesting… Infrastructure and Platform Engineering formae: Infrastructure-as-Code Platform Built for the Future - A 100% code-based, agentic IaC tool that automatically syncs code with the actual infrastructure state without needing state files or manual merging of external changes. Container (Apple Open Source) - A tool from Apple for creating and running Linux containers using secure, lightweight virtual machines on a Mac, optimized for Apple silicon.

item.title: What Edu is reading this week (Oct 20 - 26, 2025)
item.description: Another week goes by! Software & DevOps Uber Kraken - A P2P-powered Docker registry developed by Uber, designed for highly scalable and available image distribution. Xpra - Persistent remote applications for X11, MacOS, and MS Windows, known as “screen for X,” allowing disconnection and reconnection to graphical applications. pkgit - An unconventional package manager designed to compile and install packages directly from their git repository. volare - A Kubernetes volume populator project.

item.title: What Edu is Reading This Week (Oct 13-19 2025)
item.description: What Edu is Reading This Week People often ask me about the cool stuff I stumble upon during the week. So, I figured, why not share the links that caught my eye? So here we are. This is inspired by some newsletters I read such as Vermandeen’s Valuable News or Kube Today. I’m not 100% sure if I’ll be able to keep a weekly cadence; I really don’t have too much free time lately, but I’ll try!
